newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST - Polish revrepo rate seen up by end-96.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Polish revrepo rate seen up by end-96.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland's 14-day revrepo rate, last at 19.16 percent, is expected to rise to 19.18 percent by year-end, a Reuter poll of Poland's 25 biggest banks showed.

The forecast is a mean average of banks' predictions ranging from 19.00 to 19.50 percent, but eight of the polled banks did not expect the central bank to stage such operations this year and five did not expect them next year either.
In the same poll a year ago, in December 1995, banks expected the 14-day reverse repo rate at 20.41 percent on average with a range of forecats between 16.0 and 23.6 percent. @
Last month, banks had expected the 14-day rate to fall to 18.88 percent by the end of the year.
By December 1997, those banks, which expected the central bank would still stage such operations, saw the rate falling to 16.81 percent. Predictions ranged from 15.70 to 18.16 percent.
